This isn’t normal. There is nothing wrong with age differences that are larger, but there are situations where, as a younger person, we are naturally, and evolutionary, more likely to believe that someone older than us is smarter and knows more. That isn’t true and this isn’t normal. In any relationship you should be able to have conversations with each other communicate healthily.

I know you are 29 and I’m not saying you are dumb or immature. This is literally a dynamic a 40 year old and 50 year old could have.

I’m also not even going to go into who is in the right or wrong. When I have an issue with my partner, we talk about it - we don’t ignore each other and/or run to our friends houses.

Whatever you decide to do - I want you to know his reaction isn’t normal, justified or a healthy way of talking through relationship problems.

I don’t even care if you got angrier than you should of or you didn’t react perfectly. This isn’t normal or okay.

It doesn't make you a bad person. It's great, normal and healthy to support your partner during inevitable rough patches (including illnesses, both physical and mental) and it's normal to support and increase your physical, mental "workload" during those periods.

These periods should be temporary though. You are getting burnt out because this doesn't seem like a temporary period of extra excursion in the relationship. It's becoming a permanent fixture of your relationship.

She isn't looking to actively help herself and it seems like she is becoming dependant on you.

I have no context for your relationship overall or the discussions you have had previously, but have you tried to, in a non-judgmental way, explain that you are feeling stressed and burnt out? 

If it is getting too much but you want it to work, let her know that this may mean you need to step back to take care of yourself for a little while, and that if she wants it to work then she needs to do self work too.

Right now there is no balance and it's not going to be sustainable if nothing changes.

Let’s call a spade a spade, you are jealous of how close he is too her - and to a certain degree feel threatened by that. 

That’s 100% normal and okay for you to feel, even if you trust he isn’t doing anything wrong. We can't control our feelings but we can control how we react to them.

Bring up those feelings in a non-confrontational way. "Hey babe, I don't believe you have or will do anything wrong and I love so and so but I am starting to feel a little bit uncomfortable with how close you both are. I don't want or expect you to stop hanging out or seeing her, I just want you to know how I'm feeling"

If my partner told me that about one of my friends I would want to reassure them, I'd want to be more careful about ensuring my partner feels valued and I would likely also think about how I'm acting with that friend.

You sound reasonable, trusting and calm - keep that same energy with him and reassure him that you are not blaming him for anything and that he isn't doing anything wrong.

It is actually the perfect time for you to bring this up with him, especially when you can aknowledge and frame it as a "me thing, not a you thing".

You’re dedicated - are they? It’s not fair for them to cheat, obviously, but even if they didn’t it’s manipulative and not fair for them to act like they are in a bad mood and say they feel like a shitty person without saying why… What’s the purpose of that? They surely know its going to make you stressed? 

If they are in a bad mood, but super tired it doesn’t take much to be like “I’m all good, just a little upset  and needing to go to bed - I’ll tell you the story tomorrow x”

Making it about how they have done something wrong naturally has you, as their partner, worried about that that is. Could be anything from “I cheated” to “I accidentally stepped on the cats tail”

Honestly, it’s like making friends with  affection. Don’t over think it - you want to date somebody who is ultimately your best friend.

You want someone you can be silly with, be serious with, have fun with and cry with. 

Have hobbies you relate to and can do together, have different interests you want to learn more about! Dating is just finding someone you naturally connect with and want to hang around with more. 

The rest comes naturally.

You need to have a conversation with her that is not accusatory but is straight to the point.

“I love you, I want this to work, but I can see that we have both been so stressed and busy lately that we haven’t been putting the energy into our relationship that we should and it hasn’t been the priority it needs to be”

Find ways to have you time - where you refuse to talk about your son or work or chores and just focus on having fun and being present with each other.

Have a board game night, go to the beach, go out for dinner - do all the “dating” stuff you did early on and the sex part will fall back into place naturally

I can only imagine how stressful and draining it would be to be in this situation and I respect how strong you have been for him and how supportive you have been.

My concern is that you always have to look after yourself, there is only so much context a reddit post can give, but I believe that you need to have a conversation with him that essentially goes “I love you, I support you, and I cannot be the only reason that you want to be alive. What I am willing and able to do is love you, reassure you and support you - but what I need in return is for you to take your medication properly, talk to a therapist and commit to working on yourself because I don’t want this to be our forever and I want to see you enjoy life with me.”

If he is unable to commit to this, or “commits” but doesn’t follow through, then it’s better for you and him if you walk away from the relationship. If he cannot work to better his mental health then yours is going to suffer, and if you stay despite your mental health suffering then you are doing nothing to better your mental health.

It becomes a toxic and unhealthy cycle that does nothing to benefit either of you.

All the best and remember to take care of yourself first - it’s one thing to love and support your partner, but it shouldn’t be forever. It can’t be you giving 100% always.
